<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="transcriber" />{{RunningHeader|660|SPHERICAL HARMONICS|}}</noinclude>The following expressions may be given for the toroidal functions:—

{{block center|<math>\text{P}^m_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho) = \frac{(-1)^m}{\pi}\frac{\Pi(n-\frac{1}{2})}{\Pi(n-m-\frac{1}{2})}\int_0^\pi \frac{\cos m\phi}{(\cosh\rho+\sinh\rho\cos\phi)^{n+\frac{1}{2}}}d\phi</math>}}
{{block center|<math>= \frac{1}{\pi}\frac{\Pi(n+m-\frac{1}{2})}{\Pi(n-\frac{1}{2})}\int_0^\pi (\cosh\rho+\sinh\rho\cos\phi)^{n-\frac{1}{2}}\cos m\phi d\phi.</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\text{P}_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho) = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\rho \frac{\cosh n\phi}{\sqrt{2\cosh\rho-2\cosh\phi}}d\phi.</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\text{Q}_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho) = (-1)^m\frac{\Pi(n+m-\frac{1}{2})}{\Pi(n-\frac{1}{2})}\int_0^{\log\coth\frac{1}{2}\rho} (\cosh\rho</math>}}
{{block center|<math>-\sinh\rho\cosh w)^{n-\frac{1}{2}}\cosh mw dw</math>}}
{{block center|<math>= (-1)^m\frac{1}{\pi}2^m\Pi(m-\tfrac{1}{2})\Pi(-\tfrac{1}{2})\sinh{}^m\rho\int_0^\pi \frac{\cos n\phi}{(2\cosh\rho-2\cos\phi)^{m+\frac{1}{2}}}d\phi.</math>}}
The relations between functions for three consecutive values of the degree or the order are
{{block center|<math>2n\cosh\rho\text{P}^m_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho) - (n-m+\tfrac{1}{2})\text{P}^m_{n+\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho)</math>}}
{{block center|<math>-(n+m-\tfrac{1}{2})\text{P}^m_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho) = 0.</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\text{P}^{m+2}_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho) + 2(m+1)\coth\rho\text{P}^{m+1}_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho)</math>}}
{{block center|<math>-(n-m-\tfrac{1}{2})(n+m+\tfrac{1}{2})\text{P}^m_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho) = 0,</math>}}
with relations identical in form for the functions <math>\text{Q}^m_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho)</math>.

The function <math>\text{Q}_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho)</math> is expansible in the form
{{block center|<math>\frac{\Pi(n-\frac{1}{2})\Pi(-\frac{1}{2})}{\Pi(n)}e^{-(n+\frac{1}{2})\rho}\text{F}(\tfrac{1}{2},\ n+\tfrac{1}{2},\ n+1,\ e^{-2\rho}),</math>}} which is useful for calculation of the function when <math>\rho</math> is not small. <math>\text{P}_{n-\frac{1}{2}}(\cosh\rho)</math> can also be expressed in terms of <math>e^{-\rho}</math> by a somewhat complicated formula.

31. ''Ellipsoidal Harmonics''.—In order to treat potential problems in which the boundary surface is an ellipsoid, Lamé took as co-ordinates the parameters <math>\rho</math>, <math>\mu</math>, <math>\nu</math> of systems of confocal ellipsoids, hyperboloids of one sheet, and of two sheets; these co-ordinates are three roots of the equation
{{block center|<math>\frac{x^2}{t^2}+\frac{y^2}{t^2-h^2}+\frac{z^2}{t^2-k^2}=1,\ (k>h)</math>;}}
we thence find that
{{block center|<math>x=\frac{\rho\mu\nu}{hk},\ y=\frac{\sqrt{\rho^2-h^2}\sqrt{\mu^2-h^2}\sqrt{h^2-\nu^2}}{h\sqrt{k^2-h^2}},\ z=\frac{\sqrt{\rho^2-k^2}\sqrt{k^2-\mu^2}\sqrt{k^2-\nu^2}}{k\sqrt{k^2-h^2}}</math>}}
where
{{block center|<math>\infty\geqq\rho^2\geqq h^2,\ k^2\leqq\mu^2\leqq h^2</math>, and <math>k^2\geqq\nu^2\geqq 0</math>.}}

We find from these values of <math>x</math>, <math>y</math>, <math>z</math>
{{block center|<math>(dx)^2+(dy)^2+(dz)^2=\frac{(\rho^2-\mu^2)(\rho^2-\nu^2)}{(\rho^2-h^2)(\rho^2-k^2)}(d\rho)^2+\frac{(\rho^2-\mu^2)(\mu^2-\nu^2)}{(\mu^2-h^2)(k^2-\mu^2)}(d\mu)^2</math>}}
{{block center|<math>+\frac{(\rho^2-\nu^2)(\mu^2-\nu^2)}{(h^2-\nu^2)(k^2-\nu^2)}(d\nu)^2</math>,}}
and on applying the general transformation of Laplace's equation that equation becomes
{{block center|<math>(\mu^2-\nu^2)\frac{\partial^2\text{V}}{\partial\xi^2}+(\rho^2-\nu^2)\frac{\partial^2\text{V}}{\partial\eta^2}+(\rho^2-\mu^2)\frac{\partial^2\text{V}}{\partial\zeta^2}=0</math>,}}
where <math>\xi</math>; <math>\eta</math>, <math>\zeta</math> are defined by the formulae
{{block center|<math>\xi=\int_h^\rho\frac{d\rho}{\sqrt{\rho^2-h^2}\sqrt{\rho^2-k^2}},\ \eta=\int_h^\mu\frac{d\mu}{\sqrt{\mu^2-h^2}\sqrt{k^2-\mu^2}}</math>, <math>\zeta = \int_0^\nu \frac{d\nu}{\sqrt{h^2-\nu^2}\sqrt{k^2-\nu^2}},</math>}}
which are equivalent to
{{block center|<math>\rho = kdn(k\xi,\ k_1),\ \mu = kdn(\text{K}-k\eta,\ k_1),\ \nu = ksn(k\xi,\ k_1'),</math>}}
where <math>k_1^2</math>, <math>k_1'^2</math> denote the quantities <math>1-h^2/k^2</math>, <math>h^2/k^2</math> and <math>\text{K}</math> denotes the complete elliptic integral
{{block center|<math>\int_0^{\frac{1}{2}\pi} \frac{d\psi}{\sqrt{1-k_1^2\sin^2\psi}}.</math>}}
It can now be shown that Laplace's equation is satisfied by the product <math>\text{E}(\rho)\text{E}(\mu)\text{E}(\nu)</math>, where <math>\text{E}(\rho)</math> satisfies the differential equation
{{block center|<math>\frac{d^2\text{E}(\rho)}{d\xi^2} - \{n(n+1)\rho^2 - (h^2+k^2)p\}\text{E}(\rho) = 0;</math>}}
and <math>\text{E}(\mu)</math>, <math>\text{E}(\nu)</math> satisfy the equations
{{block center|<math>\frac{d^2\text{E}(\mu)}{d\eta^2} + [n(n+1)\mu^2 - p(h^2+k^2)]\text{E}(\mu) = 0,</math>}}
{{block center|<math>\frac{d^2\text{E}(\nu)}{d\zeta^2} - [n(n+1)\nu^2 - p(h^2+k^2)]\text{E}(\nu) = 0,</math>}}
where <math>n</math> and <math>p</math> are arbitrary constants. On substituting the values of the parameters <math>\xi</math>, <math>\eta</math>, <math>\zeta</math> in terms of <math>\rho</math>, <math>\mu</math>, <math>\nu</math>, we find that the equation satisfied by <math>\text{E}(\rho)</math> becomes

{{block center|<math>(\rho^2-h^2)(\rho^2-k^2)\frac{d^2\text{E}(\rho)}{d\rho^2}+\rho(2\rho^2-h^2-k^2)\frac{d\text{E}(\rho)}{d\rho}</math>}}

{{block center|<math>+\{(h^2+k^2)p-n(n+1)\rho^2\}\text{E}(\rho)=0</math>,}}

and <math>\text{E}(\mu)</math>, <math>\text{E}(\nu)</math> satisfy equations in <math>\mu</math>, <math>\nu</math> respectively of identically the same form; this equation is known as Lamé's equation.

If <math>n</math> be taken to be a positive integer, it can be shown that it is possible in <math>2n+1</math> ways so to determine <math>p</math> that the equation in <math>\text{E}(\rho)</math> is satisfied by an algebraical function of degree <math>n</math>, rational in <math>\rho</math>, <math>\surd(\rho^2-h^2)</math>, <math>\surd(\rho^2-k^2)</math>. The functions so determined are called Lamé's functions, and the <math>2n+1</math> functions of degree <math>n</math> are of one of the four forms.

{{block center|<math>\text{K}(\rho) = a_0\rho^n + a_1\rho^{n-2} + \dots</math>,}}

{{block center|<math>\text{L}(\rho) = \sqrt{\rho^2-h^2}(a_0'\rho^{n-1} + a'_1\rho^{n-3} + \dots)</math>,}}

{{block center|<math>\text{M}(\rho) = \sqrt{\rho^2-k^2}(a_0''\rho^{n-1} + a''_1\rho^{n-3} + \dots)</math>,}}

{{block center|<math>\text{N}(\rho) = \sqrt{\rho^2-k^2}\sqrt{\rho^2-h^2}(a_0'''\rho^{n-2}+a_1'''\rho^{n-4}+\dots)</math>.}}

These are the four classes of Lamé's functions of degree <math>n</math>; of the functions <math>\text{K}</math> there are <math>1+\tfrac{1}{2}n</math>, or <math>\tfrac{1}{2}(n+1)</math>, according as <math>n</math> is even or odd; of each of the functions <math>\text{L}</math>, <math>\text{M}</math>, there are <math>\tfrac{1}{2}n</math>, or <math>\tfrac{1}{2}(n-1)</math>, and of the functions <math>\text{N}</math>, there are <math>\tfrac{1}{2}n</math>, or <math>\tfrac{1}{2}(n+1)</math>.

The normal forms of solution of Laplace's equation, applicable to the space inside the ellipsoid, are the <math>2n+1</math> products <math>\text{E}(\rho)\ \text{E}(\mu)\ \text{E}(\nu)</math>. It can be shown that the <math>2n+1</math> values of <math>p</math> are real and unequal.

It can be shown that, subject to certain restrictions, a function of <math>\mu</math> and <math>\nu</math>, arbitrarily given over the surface of the ellipsoid <math>\rho = \rho_1</math>, can be expressed as the sum of products of Lamé's functions of <math>\mu</math> and <math>\nu</math>, in the form
{{block center|<math>\sum_{1}^{\infty} \sum_{s=1}^{2n+1} c^s_n \text{E}^s_n(\mu) \text{E}^s_n(\nu)</math>;}}
the potential function for the space inside the ellipsoid, which has the arbitrarily given value over the surface of the ellipsoid, is consequently
{{block center|<math>\sum\sum c^s_n \frac{\text{E}^s_n(\rho) \text{E}^s_n(\mu) \text{E}_n(\nu)}{\text{E}^s_n(\rho_1)}</math>.}}

It can be shown that a second solution of Lamé's equation is <math>\text{F}_n(\rho)</math> where
{{block center|<math>\text{F}_n(\rho) = (2n+1) \text{E}_n(\rho) \int_\rho^\infty \frac{d\rho}{\{\text{E}_n(\rho)\}^2 \sqrt{\rho^2 - h^2} \sqrt{\rho^2 - k^2}}</math>;}}
this function <math>\text{F}_n(\rho)</math> vanishes at infinity as <math>\rho^{-n-1}</math>, and is therefore adapted to the space outside the bounding ellipsoid. The external potential which has at the surface <math>\rho = \rho_1</math>, the value
{{block center|<math>\sum\sum c^s_n \text{E}^s_n(\mu) \text{E}^s_n(\nu)</math> is <math>\sum\sum c^s_n \frac{\text{F}^s_n(\rho)}{\text{F}^s_n(\rho_1)} \text{E}^s_n(\mu) \text{E}^s_n(\nu)</math>.}}

32.
